To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Internet is now a mainstream channel for many retailers.

(1) the Internet is now a significant factor in retailing, (2) the Internet has been adopted more quickly by larger retailers, and (3) the Internet is being adopted more quickly by retailers in sectors where it has been used for some time (e.g. books) than in sectors which have only recently adopted it (e.g. clothing).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) What proportion of UK retail businesses currently have a web site and how has this changed over the last four years?;
the following question: What are the trends in Internet adoption within the UK retail market?
the extent to which the Internet has been adopted by UK retailers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
whilst e-commerce adoption has increased across the UK retail sector over a four year period, it is not yet clear whether the growth will be sustained.
the Internet is not yet the major threat to traditional retailers that some commentators have suggested.
whilst e-commerce has had a major impact on some sectors and retailers, it has not yet had a major impact across all retail sectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

whilst the Internet has been adopted by a significant minority of UK retailers, the pace of adoption and the extent to which it has been used to change business processes has varied significantly between retailers.
the Internet is a significant force in retailing and that the Internet has the potential to reshape the retailing industry.
whilst there are signs that Internet technologies are having a profound impact on the retail sector, the pace of this change has slowed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Internet is a significant force in retailing and that the rate of change is accelerating.
, although there is a clear trend for growth, it is important not to over-estimate the potential impact of e-commerce on retailing in the UK.
, although the Internet may not be the panacea that many had predicted, it is clear that the Internet will have a major impact on the retail sector.
